scope: Final four-pass review of the bounded v2 Pinky/Ring native closed-grip refinement

evidence: Only the three Pinky closed/default rotations change relative to the frozen v1 candidate. All 15 open time-0 rows, every non-Pinky finger row, accepted Thumb1/2/3 rows, root, wrist, Grip, bone lengths, translations, scales, IBM, geometry, weights, NORMAL, UV, materials and all three KTX payloads remain exact.
The v2 post deltas are applied once with maximum quaternion chord error below 2.0e-8. Default skinned output equals grip time 1 exactly, and the decoded companion preserves the candidate identity.
Negative controls reject wrist translation, open-row and KTX mutation. The independent face-set policy control proves that equal pair counts with different faces would be detected.

At the held/default closed pose, all ten v1 Ring-Pinky position-weld nonadjacent crossings are removed. Every other digit-pair face set remains exactly unchanged, Pinky-to-Palm adds no contact, and no new or deeper core sample is introduced.
The fixed 24 actual Pinky3 palm-facing pad samples improve from minimum/median/P95 cord gaps of 5.0615/7.6886/9.6480 mm to 1.3924/2.2163/3.6628 mm; 17 of 24 are now within 3 mm.
The accepted Thumb3-to-Index press is unchanged: the same 24 samples remain within 1 mm, the minimum remains 0.04376 mm and actual Thumb skin displacement is zero.

At open time 0 and mid time 0.5, v2 adds no self-contact and no new or deeper solid-core sample relative to v1. The inherited source/v1 open and mid Thumb penetration is explicitly retained because the held default uses closed time 1 and this task does not alter the accepted Thumb curve.

Ring/Pinky affected face geometry remains finite with no new degenerate face or new negative normal orientation. Mixed Pinky weights move nearby Ring/Mid skin only within the independently reported bounds and do not change their matrices or face-contact sets.
The final front, back and oblique images use the exact v1 cameras, light, material scale, actual unchanged KTX pixels and formal dao; no render parameter search or visual override is involved.
The front view preserves the compact four-finger wrap and accepted Thumb clamp while the little finger now follows the handle circumference rather than ending as a detached distal hook.

The back and oblique views retain a readable Ring-Pinky seam with no fused silhouette, black triangular interpenetration or reversed surface. The Pinky tip has visible support without being forced through the cord or neighboring finger.
Wrist, cuff, hand scale, palm silhouette and handle placement remain visually unchanged from v1.
The candidate is a pure closed-pose asset delta. No SDK, app, Kotlin, HTML, formal/shared producer, Gradle, device, Blender rerender grid or Git path is modified.
The solve uses one bounded Pinky1 separation step and one supported three-hinge Pinky fit, not a broad parameter sweep or a parallel runtime correction path.

remaining_limits: This approval covers the offline held/default closed grip candidate. The source/v1 open and mid poses retain their pre-existing Thumb/core penetration; v2 proves no regression at those times rather than absolute full-curve clearance.
Finite surface samples and triangle-pair tests do not prove a continuous maximum on the nonconvex handle and finger surfaces.
Existing accepted v1 Thumb-Index and Mid-Ring contacts remain present and unchanged; this review does not reclassify or repair them.
PICO SDK animation binding, runtime rendering, device input, performance and formal publication remain Root validation work.
release_boundary: Approved as the bounded v2 right-hand asset for Root native integration review. Formal publication remains blocked until Root completes runtime/device and identity validation.
